Area.evidence_source: Narratives often moved from subjective accounts towards more general expressions of what men usually do. Typically, subjects linked their performance to masculinity. Concealing emotions and distress, they maintained, is what men do, it is male behaviour. ; You have to be man enough to ask somebody for help, but the way people look at it, you're man enough to do it yourself, so do it yourself. Don't be asking other people for help. A man should never ask for help. ; So, being a man, appearing strong, being able to manage one's life, are important reasons for not disclosing. ; The effort involved in projecting selfsufficiency while simultaneously coping with the underlying distress often required the use of alcohol and or drugs. The result was then a spiral of concealment and denial with increasing substance misuse which compounded the initial problem. ; The consequence ofconcealing this level of distress was commonly a feeling of being trapped in an impossible situation. It led the men to a position where they felt the only way out was suicide ('it was my best option').
